neighbours.label: reformulation and addition markers ('(i.e.', 'In other words', 'What's more') late in a long expository passage; the same markers in a single short sentence do not fire, so the pole needs a long preceding context
fire: Sleep researchers divide the night into cycles of about ninety minutes. Each cycle moves from light sleep into deep sleep and then into the dreaming stage. Adults need four or five full cycles to feel rested the next day. The dreaming stage (i.e., REM sleep) becomes longer toward morning, while deep sleep is concentrated in the first hours. In other words, a person who goes to bed very late loses mostly dreaming time. What's more, the loss cannot be fully repaid by sleeping longer at the weekend.

Bread dough rises because yeast feeds on the sugars in the flour. As the yeast grows it releases gas, and the gas is trapped by the stretchy network that forms when flour is kneaded with water. Bakers call the first rise the bulk fermentation. The stretchy network (i.e., gluten) is weaker in rye flour than in wheat flour. In other words, a rye loaf will always be denser than a wheat loaf. What's more, the dough is stickier, so it is harder to shape by hand.

Every resident who earns income during the year must file a return by the end of April. The form asks for wages, interest and any profit from selling property. Most people can take a fixed allowance instead of listing their costs one by one. The fixed allowance (i.e., the standard deduction) is raised each year in line with prices. In other words, a worker whose pay has not changed will owe slightly less than before. What's more, the form can now be filed online, so refunds arrive within three weeks.

Glaciers form where more snow falls in winter than melts in summer. Over many years the snow is pressed into dense ice, which begins to flow slowly downhill under its own weight. The upper part of a glacier gains ice, and the lower part loses it. The boundary between the two (i.e., the equilibrium line) moves uphill in warm decades. In other words, a glacier can shrink even when winters stay snowy. What's more, the dark rock exposed by the retreat absorbs heat, so the melting speeds up.

Chess players are ranked by a number that rises after a win and falls after a loss. The size of the change depends on how strong the opponent was expected to be. Beating a much weaker player earns almost nothing, while beating a stronger one earns a lot. The ranking number (i.e., the Elo rating) is therefore a running estimate rather than a prize. In other words, a champion who stops playing keeps a rating that may no longer be deserved. What's more, the system cannot compare players from different eras, so arguments about the greatest player never end.

Many vaccines lose their strength if they are allowed to get warm. From the factory to the clinic they travel in refrigerated trucks and insulated boxes, and each stage is checked with a thermometer. Health workers call this series of cold links the cold chain. The final stage (i.e., the trip from the district store to the village) is the hardest to control. In other words, a vaccine can be ruined in the last few hours of a journey of months. What's more, the damage is invisible, so a spoiled dose looks exactly like a good one.

Children pick up their first language without lessons, simply by hearing it spoken around them. Adults who study a second language usually rely on rules and word lists instead. Teachers have long argued about which approach works better in a classroom. Learning by exposure (i.e., immersion) gives good pronunciation but slow progress in grammar. In other words, a learner may sound fluent and still make basic mistakes. What's more, the method needs many hours a week, so it is hard to fit into a school timetable.

A suspension bridge carries its deck from two long cables that hang between tall towers. The cables pull inward on the towers and are tied down at each end in huge blocks of concrete. Thin vertical rods connect the cables to the deck below. The concrete blocks (i.e., the anchorages) must resist the whole weight of the span. In other words, a suspension bridge is only as strong as the ground at its ends. What's more, the deck is light and flexible, so strong winds can make it sway.
